rules: 1 all-in crypto pick per day, 100% deployed
Spot crypto only (BTC, ETH, SOL, and other liquid coins on Robinhood)
Rotate each 6:45am CT run — sell yesterday, buy today's best
Hard stop at entry; leverage conviction, protect downside

positions.name: Stellar Lumens
positions.catalyst: I AM BUYING STELLAR BECAUSE THE SENATE VOTES TOMORROW ON A BILL THAT NAMES XLM BY NAME, AND I GET TO OWN THE RUN-UP AND ROTATE OUT BEFORE THE VOTE RESOLVES. Senate Majority Leader Thune filed cloture on the motion to proceed to the CLARITY Act, setting a procedural vote for TUESDAY SEPTEMBER 15. The merged 616-page Senate text classifies every token as a security, a digital commodity, or a stablecoin, and XRP, XLM and HBAR are the three named examples of digital commodities. THE STRUCTURE OF THIS TRADE IS THE WHOLE POINT. The vote is tomorrow afternoon. My rotation is tomorrow at 6:45am CT. That means I hold the ANTICIPATION and I am out before the RESOLUTION. Anticipation into a binary is where the asymmetry lives; resolution is where it gets paid out or destroyed. I am deliberately buying the first half and selling the second half to my successor, and I want that stated plainly rather than dressed up as conviction about the outcome. I have no view on whether cloture clears - DeFiRate puts passage odds at 24-26% and Republicans still need roughly ten Democratic crossovers that have not been assembled. If I had to hold through the vote I would not take this position at all. THE BOARD IS GREEN TODAY AND XLM IS RUNNING AWAY WITH IT. Computed from Robinhood mark vs open_price with the day boundary set to midnight America/Chicago: XLM +3.56%, ADA +1.80%, XRP +1.68%, AAVE +0.72%, SOL +0.71%, ETC +0.54%, DOGE +0.47%, BTC +0.36%, ETH +0.05%, LINK -0.00%, BCH -0.15%, AVAX -0.35%, LTC -1.00%. XLM is beating the second-best name by 176 basis points. Yesterday I dismissed a 13bp gap as noise on thin Sunday tape and I was right to. A 176bp gap on a Monday session with real institutional participation is not noise, and the fact that the #1 and #3 names (XLM, XRP) are both tokens named in tomorrow's bill while the #2 (ADA) is not tells me the market is trading the legislative calendar rather than generic altcoin beta. STELLAR HAS A SECOND, INDEPENDENT CATALYST THAT GIVES THE DESIGNATION SUBSTANCE. On September 9 U.S. Bank announced it had run USBDC, its own USD-backed stablecoin, live on PUBLIC Stellar in a North-America-to-Europe intrabank pilot with mint, redeem, freeze and clawback all exercised. That is one of the first bank-issued stablecoins deployed on a public chain for real settlement, and it sits on a network already hosting roughly $3B of real-world assets. This matters because it means 'digital commodity' status for XLM is not a purely speculative repricing - there is an actual institutional pipeline that regulatory clarity would unlock. I am careful not to overstate it: USBDC is internal-treasury-only with no retail timeline. WHY NOT XRP, WHICH IS THE SAFER VERSION OF THE SAME TRADE. XRP is also named in the bill, has deeper liquidity, and has nine straight weeks of spot ETF inflows (~$19M last week, ~$1.7B cumulative). It is the lower-variance expression and I considered it seriously. I passed because the ETF drip is a slow structural bid, not a 24-hour catalyst, and because XRP is up only 1.68% against XLM's 3.56% - if I am buying the legislative run-up I want the name with the most torque to it, and XLM is a fraction of XRP's market cap with the same headline exposure. WHY NOT STAY IN BITCOIN, WHICH JUST WORKED. The defensive rotation paid: BTC went 76,644 to 77,915.71 for +1.66% while I slept, and none of my four pre-registered invalidations fired. But BTC's binary is the FOMC on WEDNESDAY, with 87% odds of a 25bp hike - that is two sessions away and lands after two more rotations. Holding the macro-beta major today buys me exposure to an event I will not be present for. The legislative binary is tomorrow. I would rather own the catalyst inside my window than the one outside it. WHY NOT ADA AT +1.80%. Second on the board, but it is not named in the bill and has no catalyst of its own - it is riding altcoin beta generated by the CLARITY headlines. If I want that beta I should buy its source, not its derivative. WHY NOT LTC, dead last at -1.00% and the exact name I passed on yesterday when it led. Consistent read: LTC has no catalyst, no institutional bid, no ETF complex, and its one-day rank is not information. TENTH CONSECUTIVE PASS ON SOLANA at +0.71%, mid-board with nothing specific to it. UNISWAP remains operationally disqualified - the canonical feed still prices UNI-USD as a different asset and I will not book a fill I cannot mark.
positions.driver: Closed BTC at 77,915.71 (canonical live feed, asOf 2026-09-14T10:52:55.627Z) versus entry 76,644.00 for +1,271.71 per unit, +195.69 total (+1.66%) on 0.153879 units over a one-day hold. Book rolls 11,793.87 -> 11,989.56, now +19.9% on the $10,000 inception and a new high-water mark for this book. THE DEFENSIVE ROTATION WAS RIGHT AND I WANT TO BE PRECISE ABOUT WHY, BECAUSE IT IS EASY TO LEARN THE WRONG LESSON. Yesterday I left ETH for BTC on an all-red board and called it capital preservation rather than a bet. BTC returned +1.66%; ETH over the same window went 2,474.29 to 2,514.21, which is +1.61%. I beat the asset I sold by FIVE BASIS POINTS. The rotation did not add meaningful alpha - the entire gain came from the complex turning up overnight, which I did not predict and did not claim to. What the rotation actually did was hold beta down into an unobservable weekend, which is what I said it would do. The honest scorecard is: correct process, immaterial edge, good outcome mostly attributable to tape. I should not conclude from a +1.66% day that defensive rotations generate returns. ALL FOUR PRE-REGISTERED INVALIDATIONS: NONE FIRED. (1) Monday's ETF print has not arrived - it comes tonight, so this remains untested and I am now handing it to tomorrow's run as an open question about a position I no longer hold. (2) The FOMC session is Wednesday, not yet reached. (3) BTC closing below 74,000 - did not happen, BTC rallied to 77,916 and never threatened it. (4) No dovish rip. I am exiting BTC on OPPORTUNITY COST, not on invalidation, and that is a different and weaker reason to sell. I want that on the record: the BTC thesis is intact and I am leaving it for something with a nearer catalyst. Bought XLM at 0.188489 (canonical live feed, asOf 2026-09-14T10:53:01.631Z). CROSS-CHECK PASSED ON BOTH LEGS: Robinhood mark at 05:53:07 CT was 77,933.00 for BTC (2.2bp from my exit) and 0.18886175 for XLM (20bp from my fill). The XLM gap is wider in relative terms but the Robinhood book on XLM is 0.1870325 bid / 0.190691 ask - a 190bp spread - so 20bp between two feeds sits comfortably inside the quoted market and is not a stale-price signature. Both stamps are within a minute of run time. Cache-buster and asOf verification applied on every canonical call, now permanent procedure since the 1,742.98 stale-ETH incident. SIZING AND RISK BUDGET: 63,608.794306 XLM at 0.188489 = $11,989.56 deployed, 100% of book. Alt-tier 10% stop at 0.169640. I chose 10% rather than 12% specifically because this position carries binary headline risk during the hold - a whip-count leak does not need to be large to move a small-cap name, and I want the stop close enough to matter on a normal trading move even knowing it will not save me in a gap. METHOD NOTE, CARRIED FORWARD AND CONFIRMED WORKING: canonical Vercel feed for the FILL, Robinhood open_price anchored to midnight America/Chicago for the BOARD. The canonical proxy still returns previousClose as null for every crypto symbol, so it can give a level but not a change. Every percentage above is computed by me from those two sources. One operational wrinkle today: the canonical endpoint returned an EMPTY BODY on a 13-symbol request but responded correctly when split into batches of four. Future runs should request the board in batches of four or fewer rather than treating an empty response as an outage. YESTERDAY'S STRUCTURAL RULE, APPLIED. I wrote that a flow-based thesis should not be carried through a weekend because the flow data cannot print. Today's trade is the mirror image and I am applying the same logic in the other direction: an EVENT-based thesis should be sized to end BEFORE the event, because the moment the event resolves the thesis has no remaining informational edge and becomes a coin flip. Both rules come from the same principle - hold a position only while its evidence base is live and testable.
positions.risks: THE MODAL OUTCOME OF TOMORROW'S VOTE IS FAILURE, AND THE MARKET MAY FIGURE THAT OUT WHILE I STILL OWN THIS. Passage odds are 24-26%. Republicans need roughly ten Democratic crossovers that had not been assembled as of four days before the vote. Whip counts leak, senators announce positions, and a single 'we don't have the votes' headline from a Democratic bloc could take XLM down hard TODAY - inside my holding window, before I get to execute the clean rotation-before-resolution plan the whole trade is built on. My structural edge assumes the news arrives tomorrow afternoon. Nothing guarantees that. I AM BUYING THE STRONGEST NAME ON THE BOARD AFTER IT HAS ALREADY MOVED 3.56%. That is chasing, and I should call it that. The run-up I claim to be buying is partly a run-up I have already missed, and the 176bp relative-strength gap I am treating as signal is exactly the kind of figure that mean-reverts on a name this size. If the CLARITY trade was put on last week by people with better legislative sourcing than mine, I am the late money. XLM IS THE THINNEST THING I HAVE OWNED IN THIS BOOK AND THE ORDER BOOK PROVES IT. Robinhood quotes 0.1870325 bid against 0.190691 ask - a 190 basis point spread on a $12,000 position. Yesterday I rejected LTC partly for lack of order-book depth and today I am buying a name with a visibly wide market. The distinction I am drawing is that XLM has a catalyst and institutional integration that LTC does not, but the liquidity criticism I leveled at LTC applies here too and I do not want to pretend otherwise. Exit slippage is a real cost on this position in a way it was not on BTC. THE 10% STOP AT 0.169640 WILL NOT PROTECT ME AGAINST THE RISK I ACTUALLY TOOK. Legislative headlines gap small-cap tokens; they do not walk them down through levels. If cloture visibly fails, XLM trades through 0.1696 rather than at it. The stop is a discipline against ordinary drift, not against the binary, and the binary is the reason I am here. I am accepting genuine gap risk and the honest mitigation is the short holding period, not the stop. I AM LEAVING A WORKING POSITION FOR AN UNPROVEN ONE. BTC just made me 1.66%, none of my invalidations fired, and Monday evening's ETF print - the single data point that would have resolved the BTC-versus-ETH flow question I have been chasing for three sessions - lands tonight, after I have already sold. I will never learn the answer to my own open question because I rotated before it printed. That is a recurring cost of a daily-rotation mandate and today it bites directly. I HAVE NOW ROTATED SEVEN TIMES IN SEVEN DAYS. Every rotation costs spread, and today's spread is the widest yet. The lowest-variance action was to sit in BTC into the FOMC and skip the legislative lottery ticket entirely. I rejected it because owning a dated catalyst inside my window beats owning an undated one outside it, but a reader should know that 'do nothing' was a defensible alternative that I turned down. STRUCTURAL INVALIDATION, PRE-REGISTERED FOR TOMORROW: (1) The Senate cloture vote FAILS or is pulled from the calendar - in that case the entire reason for owning XLM is gone and the position comes off at any price, no defending it as a 'stablecoin infrastructure' story I did not buy it for; or (2) credible whip-count reporting emerges today showing Democratic crossovers below the needed threshold - same treatment, the thesis dies on the news, not on the vote; or (3) XLM's lead over XRP compresses to under 50bp, meaning the market is trading the bill generically rather than favoring the smaller named beneficiary, which removes my reason for choosing XLM over the more liquid name; or (4) XLM trades below 0.1800, breaking beneath the level this rally launched from and turning the breakout into a failed one. Any one ends the position regardless of price. Hard stop 0.169640 (-10%, alt-tier).
